claim: Process casualty reports through PCR submission within 8 hours.
quote: The timeframe for submitting the required voice report has been shortened from one hour to 30 minutes. Additionally, the relevant casualty template must be submitted
fix: Units give MFPC a voice report as soon as they know, and in garrison within 30 minutes. The PCR template goes to casualty.section@usmc.mil within one hour. The 8 hour figure is the notification goal under MCO 3040.4 chapter 4. Fix lines 4, 30, 48, 52, 68, 88 and 96 and the IGMC checklist wording.

claim: MCAAT and IGMC inspect PCR timeliness against an 8-hour standard.
quote: The timeframe for submitting the required voice report has been shortened from one hour to 30 minutes.
fix: Inspectors check the 30 minute voice report and the one hour template. Cite MARADMIN 186/25.

claim: The 8-hour window drives the PNOK notification chain.
quote: The Marine Corps’ goal is to accomplish all required notifications within 8 hours of learning of the casualty incident.
fix: The 8 hours is the goal for finishing notification, measured from learning of the casualty. It is not a PCR window.

claim: Submit the PCR through the casualty reporting chain per chapter 3 (DCIPS-Forward era process).
quote: The DCIPS-PCR spreadsheet method replaces DCIPS-8.0 (also known as DCIPS-Forward) as the sole authorized method for submitting Personnel Casualty Reports (PCR)
fix: Use the DCIPS-PCR spreadsheet. Method One covers a single casualty, Method Two covers five or more. Email to casualty.section@usmc.mil. The web portal is not accepted.

claim: CACO runs in-person notification. Telephonic notification only when in-person is not possible.
quote: The PNOK and SNOK, defined in Chapter 1, will be notified telephonically by MFPC.
fix: In-person notification covers the deceased, DUSTWUN and missing. For wounded, seriously ill or injured and VSI Marines, MFPC notifies by telephone and a CACO is added on request.

claim: SGLV 8283 is the Claim for Death Gratuity.
quote: A pre-populated DD Form 397 (Claim Certification and Voucher for Death Gratuity Payment) and Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) will then be faxed or emailed to
fix: The death gratuity claim is DD Form 397, completed with the CACO and processed by MFPC through DFAS. SGLV 8286 is the SGLI election. The archive lists no SGLV 8283.

claim: Missing Marines pay continues per DoDFMR Vol 7A Chapter 34 paragraph 4.0.
fix: DoDFMR Vol 7A chapters 34 to 36 and 47 are not in the archive. Verify the chapter numbers against the current FMR.

claim: The CACO is designated by the casualty branch.
quote: the reporting unit will assign a CACO and provide MFPC with the information
fix: If the NOK lives near the parent command the reporting unit assigns the CACO after coordination with MFPC. Otherwise MFPC tasks the nearest activity.

claim: The CACO must be senior to or peer with the deceased.
quote: When possible, the CACO should be of equal or higher grade than the casualty.
fix: Equal or higher grade is a preference. The order requires an SNCO, warrant or officer, not a relative or close friend, not leaving within six months, and trained under chapter 2.

claim: T&R events 0102-OPER-1002, 0111-OPER-2001 and 0102-GENA-2111 map to the workflow.
quote: 0111-OPER-2001:  Process Personnel Casualty Report (PCR)

claim: Casualty chapter and paragraph cites (chapter 3 casualty reporting, chapter 4 casualty assistance calls).
quote: Chapter 3 CASUALTY REPORTING

claim: Per chapter 4 section 2 paragraph 2, the CACO must be senior to or peer with the deceased.
quote: When possible, the CACO should be of equal or higher grade than the casualty.
fix: Assigning a CACO is chapter 4 section 1 paragraph 2, and the grade rule is a preference.

claim: The rank rule is mandatory.
quote: When possible, the CACO should be of equal or higher grade than the casualty.
fix: Change to should. Add the mandatory limits: SNCO or above, not a relative or close friend, not leaving within six months.

claim: The commander signs the CACO assignment order and the S-1 briefs duties per section 2 paragraph 3.
quote: Upon assignment, MFPC assumes direct control of the CACO
fix: Section 1 covers CACO assignment. After assignment MFPC controls the CACO. The commander selects the CACO but the order requires no signed assignment order.

claim: CACO candidates must have completed Casualty Assistance Program Training per chapter 2.
quote: Be trained in accordance with requirements in Chapter 2.

claim: Training is cited as chapter 2 section 2.
quote: Casualty Assistance Program Training
fix: Chapter 2 has numbered paragraphs, no sections. Cite chapter 2 paragraph 2.

claim: Reassignment of responsibilities is chapter 4 section 2 paragraph 4.
quote: Reassignment of Responsibilities
fix: Section 1 paragraph 4.

claim: Coordinate LTAP and RSP from chapter 4 for CACO workflow.
quote: Long Term Assistance Program

claim: Notification conduct is chapter 4 section 3.
quote: Phase I: Notification and Condolences
fix: Notification is section 2 (Phase I). Section 3 is mortuary affairs and funeral honors. Fix every section and paragraph cite on this page.

claim: In-person notification is the standard and telephonic or message applies only when in-person is not feasible.
quote: The PNOK and SNOK, defined in Chapter 1, will be notified telephonically by MFPC.
fix: Deceased, DUSTWUN and missing get in-person notification. Ill and injured get telephone notification from MFPC.

claim: The S-1 officer coordinates notification timing with the HQMC Casualty Section.
quote: All casualty assistance calls will be coordinated through MFPC to ensure simultaneous notification of PNOK and SNOK.
fix: MFPC coordinates notification timing. Reword the S-1 role.

claim: PNOK and SNOK come from DD Form 93 and MCTFS dependency records.
quote: The DD Form 93, when completed, for military personnel is an official record of the beneficiaries designated to receive death gratuity and pay allowances.

claim: Notification goal of 8 hours with hours of notification 0500 to 2400.
quote: Hours of notification are 0500-2400, unless directed by the MFPC.
fix: Add the 8 hour goal and the 0500 to 2400 window to the page. It states neither.

claim: The commander authorizes notification dispatch.
quote: Notification will be made on reportable casualties
fix: Notification is directed by MFPC. Remove the commander authorization step.

claim: The S-1 prepares and submits the PCR within the timeline per chapter 3.
quote: must be prepared and transmitted immediately upon knowledge and verification of the incident.
fix: The PCR goes out immediately on knowledge and verification, with an advance copy emailed to MCOC and MF before release. MARADMIN 186/25 sets the 30 minute voice report and one hour template.

claim: Prepare DD Form 1300 when death is confirmed (S-1 workflow step).
quote: The DD Form 1300 is the military equivalent of a civil death certificate and will only be produced by MFPC in all required cases.
fix: MFPC produces the DD Form 1300. Units do not prepare it. Remove from the unit workflow and the pitfalls list. Cite chapter 7 section 2 paragraph 3.

claim: PCR submissions use DCIPS and the DD Form 93 card.
quote: The DCIPS-PCR spreadsheet method replaces DCIPS-8.0 (also known as DCIPS-Forward) as the sole authorized method
fix: Use the DCIPS-PCR spreadsheet emailed to casualty.section@usmc.mil.

claim: Select the PCR type per chapter 3 section 2 paragraph 1.

fix: PCR types are in paragraph 2. Paragraph 1 is PCR Requirements.

claim: PCR distribution is chapter 3 section 2 paragraph 3.
quote: PCR Distribution

claim: Nonreportable casualties are in section 3.
quote: Nonreportable Casualties
fix: Nonreportable casualties are chapter 3 section 1 paragraph 3. Section 3 is Reports to Higher Headquarters.

claim: Supplemental PCRs follow the initial report.
quote: Supplemental PCRs will be generated every 30 days to provide MFPC and the next of kin with a status of investigations until completed.
fix: Add the 30 day supplemental rule and the 24 hour supplemental after an investigation completes.

claim: SGLV 8283 is the Claim for Death Gratuity form.
quote: A pre-populated DD Form 397 (Claim Certification and Voucher for Death Gratuity Payment)
fix: Death gratuity is claimed on DD Form 397 through the CACO and MFPC.

claim: The beneficiary submits SGLV 8283 to claim SGLI.
quote: Servicemembers’ Group Life Insurance (SGLI)
fix: SGLI claims run through the CACO and the SGLI administrator. The order does not name SGLV 8283. Cite the SGLI claim form from the current VA and OSGLI guidance.

claim: Benefits and Entitlements Visit is chapter 4 section 6 paragraph 2.
quote: Benefits and Entitlements Visit
fix: Phase III is section 4 and the visit is paragraph 2. Section 6 is mobilization.

claim: Refresh SGLV 8286 annually and at every life event.
quote: Ensure that an administrative audit of the Record of Emergency Data (RED) (DD Form 93) and Servicemembers’ Group Life Insurance Election and Certificate (SGLV 8286)
fix: Commanders audit the RED and SGLV 8286 on check in and at set events. Cite the order list rather than an annual rule.

claim: Death gratuity beneficiary chain follows DoD rules with member designation per SGLV 8286.
quote: Marines can designate a beneficiary(ies) to receive up to 100% of the DG.
fix: Members designate death gratuity beneficiaries on the DD Form 93 in 10 percent increments. Without a full designation the by-law order applies: spouse, children, parents, executor, other next of kin.

claim: Death gratuity is an immediate payment per DoDFMR Vol 7A chapter 36.
fix: DoDFMR Vol 7A chapters 35 to 36 are not in the archive. Confirm the chapter.

claim: During combat operations or a mass casualty event the MEF and MEF MSEs keep a 24-hour capability to process casualty reports.
quote: During combat operations or a mass casualty event, the MEF and MEF MSE(s) will maintain a 24-hour capability to process casualty reports

fix: Cite the order assigning the G-1. Paragraph 6 assigns the command.

claim: Mass casualty reporting uses a Method Two template for five or more casualties.
quote: This method is specifically designed for the initial reporting of mass casualty events involving five or more casualties.
fix: Add Method Two. After the initial report each casualty needs an individual Method One report.

claim: MFPC is the Marine Force Personnel Center.
quote: The Casualty Section, Military Personnel and Recreation, Personal and Family Readiness Division (MFPC)
fix: MFPC is the HQMC Casualty Section. Fix the acronym on every casualty page.

claim: LTAP transitions assistance from the CACO to HQMC LTAP representatives at case maturity.
quote: over time, MFPC shifts the focus of personal assistance to the NOK from the in-person support of the CACO to that of a permanent resource

claim: LTAP timing is judged by the case with no set date.
quote: A LTAP representative at MFPC will review decedent case files approximately sixty days after death.
fix: Add the benchmarks. LTAP reviews the file about 60 days after death. A letter goes to the PNOK at 60 days and another at one year. A CACO usually finishes admin duties in 30 to 60 days.

claim: LTAP transition is required at case maturity.
quote: Dependent upon the determination of the LTAP, the CACO may continue to be the primary point of contact for the NOK.
fix: LTAP decides whether the CACO continues. Reword.

fix: RSP sits in section 6 (casualty assistance during and after mobilization). It is a Reserve pool of Peacetime/Wartime Support Team personnel. MARFORRES trains PWST IMA billets. Remove the S-1 activation and commander assignment.
